scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: PC0 (20.1.1.x, on the OSPF side) reports it cannot reach
PC12 (120.1.1.x, on the EIGRP side) across the core -- they suspect the OSPF-to-
EIGRP redistribution at R11 broke, or that an interior link on the path is down.
Please confirm the cross-core fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk-reported fault — PC0 (20.1.1.x) unable to reach PC12 (120.1.1.x) — is not confirmed by any current or historical evidence. A topology-wide reachability test shows 0 % packet loss in both directions, and every subsystem on the pc0→r1→r11→r12→pc12 data path is healthy.

OSPF-to-EIGRP redistribution at R11 is functioning correctly: R11 runs EIGRP AS 100 (neighbours r12/112.1.1.2 and r13/103.1.1.2 both active) and its OSPF process carries `redistribute eigrp`, which is delivering 120.0.0.0/8 into the OSPF domain — R1's FIB confirms `120.0.0.0/8 via OSPF metric 20 → 111.1.1.2 (r11)`. The reverse path from R12 to the OSPF side is handled by a pre-installed kernel default route (`0.0.0.0/0 via 112.1.1.1`) on R12, which forwards to R11 and on through OSPF. All physical interfaces are up (infra_sweep clean), no traffic-shaping is in place (tc_snapshot clean), and no device is under CPU or socket pressure (pressure_sweep clean).

The only configuration oddity found is R8 declaring OSPF area 0.0.0.2 with no peers — its BB segment is a stub with no attached devices and its loopbacks are advertised into the backbone via a functioning virtual-link to R4 (VLINK0 adj=1). This is an unusual but non-breaking design that has no effect on the pc0↔pc12 path. R13 has no ospfd, which is expected for an EIGRP-only leaf. No flap scripts, daemon failures, or adjacency-reset logs were found to support a transient fault claim.

Root cause: The reported symptom is unconfirmed — the cross-core path is fully operational and no fault mechanism exists. Fix: no corrective action required; the ticket may reflect a transient lab-startup condition that resolved once EIGRP adjacencies converged.
